page.title: Choosing a Virtual Events Platform: Decisions First
page.description: Learn the first decisions to make when selecting a virtual events platform, including roles, run of show, rehearsal, escalation, and asset timing.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual events platforms?
page.definition: Virtual events platforms are software suites that host live, recorded, or hybrid experiences for audiences ranging from a few dozen to tens of thousands, providing streaming, registration, engagement tools, analytics, and integration with marketing systems. They also manage speaker workflows, audience interaction, and post‑event reporting.
page.quick_answer: Decide the event format, audience size, and internal ownership before evaluating any platform.

sections.h2: Which event format and audience size drive the platform choice?

blocks.p: The format (webinar, multi‑track conference, hybrid summit) and the expected attendee count determine whether you need a simple streaming studio or an enterprise suite.

ul: Single‑track webinar up to a few hundred attendees
Multi‑track conference with breakout rooms and networking
Hybrid summit requiring on‑site AV sync and remote streaming
Large‑scale virtual expo with booths and sponsor analytics

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show, rehearsals, and escalation on the day?

blocks.p: Assign a single show caller to own the run of show, a speaker manager for rehearsals, and a platform operator for live escalation, so no task falls through the cracks.

ol: Create the master run of show document
Schedule a full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before
Run a technical check sixty minutes before go‑live
Activate the backup stream if the primary fails
Confirm replay delivery within twenty four to forty eight hours

sections.h2: What cost model matches your budget and procurement process?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate the market: per‑host licences tied to attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly subscriptions, and annual contracts negotiated with sales teams.

sections.h2: How early must assets and speaker briefs be locked to avoid last‑minute risk?

blocks.p: Lock speaker decks, branded templates, lower‑third graphics, and Q&A scripts at least two to three weeks before the live date to give production time for review and encoding.

ul: Final slide deck approved by brand
Speaker brief with timing and tech requirements
Q&A moderation guide and fallback questions

sections.h2: Which integration and analytics capabilities are non‑negotiable for post‑event follow‑up?

blocks.p: The platform must push registration data into your CRM, feed engagement metrics to your analytics dashboard, and export attendee lists for marketing automation without manual CSV work.

ul: Native CRM connector for HubSpot or Salesforce
Real‑time engagement API for GA4 or custom dashboards
Automated replay link delivery via email platform
Attendee scoring export for lead routing
Single sign‑on support for corporate directories

faq.q: How long does it take to launch a webinar on a new platform?
faq.a: A simple webinar can move from brief to live in three to four weeks when the run of show, speaker briefs, and assets are ready early and the team completes a full rehearsal on the actual platform and a technical check sixty minutes before go live.

faq.q: What is the difference between a platform licence and a production crew?
faq.a: A platform licence gives you the software to stream and manage attendees, while a production crew provides the show caller, camera operators, encoder, backup stream, and live moderation that turn the software into a polished event. West Peek Productions supplies the crew on the platform you choose.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Send the edited replay within twenty four to forty eight hours after the live session while the content is still fresh and the audience is most likely to click. Include key clips and a short survey to capture feedback and drive next‑step actions.

faq.q: Can I run a hybrid summit on a self‑serve monthly plan?
faq.a: Hybrid summits usually need on‑site AV coordination, dedicated platform operators, and a backup stream, which exceed the limits of a self‑serve monthly plan and typically require an annual contract with enterprise support. Plan for six to eight weeks of preparation and a full rehearsal on the actual platform before the event.
